s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent painful skin lesions with ulceration and systemic inflammation
salient_findings: Painful pimple-like bumps on bilateral lower legs
Ulcers with central eschars and dusky gray borders
key_facts: Patient is a young black woman
Presented with chills and bilateral lower extremity swelling
Recent course of trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole for methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus
Medical history includes treatment with methimazole and atenolol
Laboratory tests show elevated CRP and ESR
Normal C3 and C4 complement levels
ANA titer 1:80
P-ANCA titer 1:20
Anti-myeloperoxidase (MPO) titer 141 U
Anti-SSA/Ro antibodies level 120 U
Punch biopsy shows mid- and deep dermal lymphohistiocytic infiltrate with neutrophils and focal abscess
Second biopsy shows intraepidermal and dermal perivascular neutrophilic infiltrate with necrosis of vessel walls

shortlist.label: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated CRP, ESR, and ANCA titer, consistent with systemic vasculitis

shortlist.label: Microscopic polyangiitis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated ANCA titer and presence of necrotizing vasculitis on biopsy

shortlist.label: Cutaneous leukocytoclastic vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of leukocytoclastic vasculitis on biopsy and skin lesions with ulceration

shortlist.label: Erythema induratum
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of painful skin lesions with ulceration and systemic inflammation

shortlist.label: Polyarteritis nodosa
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of systemic inflammation and vasculitis on biopsy, although less likely due to lack of medium-sized artery involvement

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with painful lesions, chills, and bilateral lower extremity swelling, along with laboratory results showing elevated CRP and ESR, and positive anti-myeloperoxidase (MPO) titer, is consistent with microscopic polyangiitis. The biopsy findings of intraepidermal and dermal perivascular neutrophilic infiltrate with necrosis of vessel walls also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis
rejected.why: The absence of granulomas in the biopsy and the lack of upper respiratory tract involvement make this diagnosis less likely

rejected.label: Cutaneous leukocytoclastic vasculitis
rejected.why: While the patient has vasculitis, the presence of anti-MPO antibodies and the systemic nature of the symptoms suggest a more systemic disease

rejected.label: Erythema induratum
rejected.why: The patient's lesions do not have the characteristic features of erythema induratum, and the biopsy findings do not support this diagnosis

rejected.label: Polyarteritis nodosa
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and biopsy findings are not consistent with polyarteritis nodosa, which typically involves medium-sized arteries and does not have the same level of systemic inflammation
